- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via isOverrideActor (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4933069f51e904af49f9287c15179f6047cbf62c` — the merge of head `24b6c9a58cd8bb15632a5745b8325488ca8dada0` into base `33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4933069f51e904af49f9287c15179f6047cbf62c && git checkout 4933069f51e904af49f9287c15179f6047cbf62c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 24b6c9a58cd8bb15632a5745b8325488ca8dada0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 && git merge --no-ff 24b6c9a58cd8bb15632a5745b8325488ca8dada0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the record below. An isolated reviewer rendered it on this head at the contract-review tier.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `350bc40b6e86baf76d6342c26b96d63a3f9311c0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/pending-approver-read-grant.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-column-creation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md (all read on `main` or at the head, none reviewed)

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change comes from one predicate, `ApprovalService.isOverrideActor`. Every caller of it was read at the head.

- **Override doors (approve, reject, recall, reassign): right.** A tenant administrator acting on a request with no organization under `group` or `isolated` moves from admitted to `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`. The refusal comes from `refuseUnreadableRequest`, before any status, slate or submitter test.
- **Other act doors (send back, resubmit, remind, request info, comment): right.** The same caller used to pass the readability check through the override and get the door's own answer. It now gets the missing-id answer.
- **`viewer.can_override`: right.** It uses the same predicate on the row's organization, so the flag and the gate still agree.
- **The three callers that pass the actor's own organization (`visibleRequestIdsFor`, `visibleRequestIds`, the pending-approver read grant): right in direction, undeclared.** A tenant-administrator context with no active organization under a wall moves from the unrestricted view to the participant set. See ③ and ④.
- **`single`: unchanged, right.** `postureEnforcesWall('single')` is false, so the tenant arm still admits. This is pinned on the four override doors.
- **Unknown posture (the provider answers nothing): unchanged, right per answer A.** The predicate answers "no wall".
- **Platform administrator and system context: unchanged, right.** Both arms return before the new line.
- **A request that carries an organization: unchanged, right.** The comparison is the old one, with the null arm removed.
- **Public surface: none moved.** No export, schema key or `IApprovalService` member changes. `organizationWallStands` is private. The new runtime import of `normalizeTenancyPosture` and `postureEnforcesWall` comes from a package already in `dependencies`.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 prescribes. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. That is the right arm for an accept-set that only shrinks.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- The changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, who moves, and the fix. The fix was checked against the tree: `os migrate organization-ownership` takes `--apply --plan-file --backup-taken`, and the ceremony's inventory lists `sys_approval_request` with fate attribution.
- The PR body carries the `Skills-docs:` line a narrowing owes.
- `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question, answer A (an unknown posture reads as unwalled): answered, holds.**
  - It matches `vetOrganizationClaim` for an absent posture, and ADR-0131 D9's lean-embedding note (no organization object, no wall).
  - The real tenancy service always answers a valid posture.
  - The package's existing harnesses construct the service with no provider and no request organization, so A is pinned incidentally.
- **The other `isOverrideActor` callers: answered by reading, not measured.**
  - The shared resolver states that with no active organization, no organization-scoped grant applies. The `TENANT_ADMIN` rung derives only from such a grant.
  - So a tenant-administrator context without a tenant does not come out of the shared resolver; only a hand-built context can carry it. The new denial runs in the wall's own direction. [detail held by the security seat]
  - It stays unpinned and absent from the changeset: a should-fix, in ④.
- **Changeset level `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: answered, right** (②).
- **Dogfood battery not measured: ESCALATED; CI does not answer it.**
  - The run on this head is a `pull_request` run. `Dogfood Regression Gate (${{ matrix.shard }}/3)` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `skipped` by design (AGENTS.md "Two speeds"), and the green `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate counted no shard.
  - No check-run on this head executed the new dogfood case, or any other dogfood file.
  - So the case is unmeasured everywhere, and by reading it cannot pass (④, must-fix).

### ④ Design judgment

**Against the spec, the narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real.**
- ADR-0131 D1 says NULL is not a state, and nothing reads a NULL tenant value as an owner. The removed arm read a NULL organization as "every organization's administrator".
- D9 stamps or refuses new writes, so the affected rows are those on stores built before the tenant column became NOT NULL.
- No declared capability is taken from a consumer: the override was only ever declared "within their own org".

Attempts to break it:
- **A door that still admits: none found.** All nine act doors reach `refuseUnreadableRequest`, directly or through `loadPendingRow`. The action-token and SLA paths run as the system by design. The record-lock hooks have no administrator bypass. The `admin_rescue` slate answers nobody for a request with no organization.
- **Over-refusal: none found.** The platform administrator and the system return before the new line. An organization's own administrator on its own request takes the unchanged comparison.
  - One consequence, which the changeset states: under a wall, an organization's administrator can no longer release their own record locked by a request with no organization. Only the platform administrator or the system can, until the ceremony attributes the row.
- **`single` changed: no.**
- **A refusal that differs from a missing id's: none found.** The throw is the same `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` with the caller's id. The validations that run before the row load are the same for both ids.
- **List and read paths beyond the ruling: one.** See should-fix 2 below.

Findings:

1. **Must-fix: the new dogfood case cannot plant its fixture on the harness store.**
   - The case sets `organization_id` to null on `sys_approval_request` through `driver.update`, on a fresh `bootStack` in-memory SQLite store.
   - On that store the driver creates the tenant column NOT NULL (ADR-0131 D1 note; `createColumn` with `tenantColumn`), and `sys_approval_request` declares `organization_id` with tenancy on.
   - `main`'s own QA checklist (`approvals.json`, knownGaps) records that exact UPDATE refused with `NOT NULL constraint failed`.
   - Sibling suites on the same harness relax the column first with `relaxTenantColumns` (`pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts`), for example `sharing-rule-org-less-caller.dogfood.test.ts`. This case does not.
   - This is a reading, not a run: no local run and no check-run on this head has executed the file. So the door-level claim in the PR body rests on nothing measured, and the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` would go red in the queue.
   - Fix: relax the tenant column on the approval tables before planting, and report a measured green run of the file on the new head.
2. **Should-fix: the read-side consequence is neither declared nor pinned.** The same line narrows the list, read and pending-approver-grant answers for a tenant-administrator context with no active organization under a wall. Add one pin per caller on a hand-built context, and one sentence in the changeset.
3. **Nit: the docblock overstates agreement with `vetOrganizationClaim`.** `organizationWallStands` normalizes the posture, so an unrecognized non-empty string reads as unwalled, while `vetOrganizationClaim` reads the same string as walled. The two agree only for an absent posture. The real tenancy service never emits such a value.
4. **Nit: the list-door pin does not discriminate.** It stays green under the ablation, because the list's organization filter already excluded the row. It is a control, not a pin of this change.
5. **Nit: a stale statement of the old rule.** `approval-revise.test.ts` still says "a null-org request is global". That now holds only without a wall.

**VERDICT: FAIL**
